ai.definition: Autonomous AI Agents are LLM-powered entities capable of performing complex tasks autonomously, including using external tools, browsing the web, and executing multi-step plans without human intervention.
ai.howItWorks: These agents leverage ReAct prompting loops to generate actions based on a task description. They use tool-use APIs for interaction with the environment and long-term memory stored in vector databases to maintain context across interactions.
ai.problemSolved: They address the need for automation in complex, multi-step tasks that require access to external tools and information, such as corporate workflows and software development processes.
ai.manufacturing: Manufacturing involves developing LLMs, integrating tool-use APIs, and setting up vector databases. This process requires significant computational resources but can be scaled with cloud services.
ai.buildProcess: The build process includes training the AI on large datasets, fine-tuning it using ReAct prompting loops, integrating with external tools via API, and deploying the agent in a production environment.
ai.costDrivers: Cost drivers include the cost of computational resources for training and operation, data labeling, and integration with existing systems. These costs can be high but are mitigated by cloud services.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: growing adoption in specific verticals like software development and corporate workflows, with potential for broader application as technology matures.
ai.regulation: Currently unregulated, but may face regulatory scrutiny as they become more prevalent in sensitive applications. Privacy concerns regarding data storage and usage are a key issue.
ai.risks: Risk of misuse, privacy breaches, and potential job displacement due to automation. Dependence on stable internet connectivity and robust API access is also a risk.
ai.profitability: Profitability depends on the specific use case; early adopters in high-value industries may see significant cost savings and efficiency gains.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely focus on improving generalization, reducing dependency on internet access, and enhancing security measures to protect data privacy.
ai.energyRequirements: Field units draw low hundreds of watts; fabrication is energy-intensive due to vacuum baking and high-performance computing requirements.

glossary.def: A method for generating actions based on a task description, using a loop of feedback to refine the agent's understanding and actions.
A type of AI model trained on large datasets that can generate human-like text and perform various language-related tasks.
Application Programming Interfaces allowing the autonomous agent to interact with external tools and services.

subsystems.name: Model backbone
subsystems.role: the language model that reads context and decides the next action.

subsystems.name: Control loop
subsystems.role: repeatedly plans, acts and observes until the task is done.

subsystems.name: Tool layer
subsystems.role: lets the agent actually change things outside the model.

subsystems.name: Memory and retrieval
subsystems.role: stores what happened and fetches relevant knowledge.

subsystems.name: Guardrails and permissions
subsystems.role: bounds what the agent may do without a human.

subsystems.name: Evaluation and observability
subsystems.role: measures whether runs succeed and why they fail.

buildSteps.title: Choose and test the base model
buildSteps.detail: Pick a model whose context window, tool-calling ability and cost fit the job; benchmark it on the real tasks, not generic chat tests.

buildSteps.title: Define the tools
buildSteps.detail: Write a small, well-documented set of callable functions — search, read file, send message, query database — each with typed inputs and outputs, since vague tool descriptions are a main cause of wrong actions.

buildSteps.title: Write the loop and prompt
buildSteps.detail: Specify the system prompt, the reason-act-observe cycle, and the rules for when to stop, retry or ask a human.

buildSteps.title: Add memory
buildSteps.detail: Embed past interactions and documents into a vector store so the agent can retrieve relevant facts instead of relying on the whole history fitting in context.

buildSteps.title: Sandbox execution
buildSteps.detail: Run generated code and network calls in an isolated environment with narrowly scoped credentials, so a mistake cannot delete production data or leak secrets.

buildSteps.title: Build the evaluation harness
buildSteps.detail: Create a test set of representative tasks with pass/fail checks, then run every prompt or model change against it to catch regressions.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with human checkpoints
buildSteps.detail: Start in a supervised mode where irreversible actions need approval, log every step, and widen autonomy only as measured success rates justify it.

pathway.milestone: single-domain agents that draft, code, search and file tickets under supervision
pathway.unlocks: real time savings on bounded, reversible tasks.

pathway.milestone: standard tool and permission protocols so agents can cross between systems
pathway.unlocks: agents that finish a workflow end to end instead of one step.

pathway.milestone: verifiable planning, where the agent checks its own intermediate results
pathway.unlocks: longer, less supervised runs with fewer compounding errors.

pathway.milestone: organisations running many cooperating agents with audited permissions
pathway.unlocks: autonomous business processes — contingent on solving reliability, security and accountability.
